sites.name: Mars 6 lander
sites.coordNote: Impact location published by NASA GISS Mars24 lander catalogue (19.42 W, 23.90 S); Soviet descent data ceased near the surface.
sites.summary: Mars 6 transmitted for 224 seconds during descent, then crashed at 23.9 S, 19.42 W in 1974 — its wreck is still in Samara Valles.
narrative: Mars 6 launched in August 1973 as part of the Soviet Mars program. On 12 March 1974 it entered the atmosphere and transmitted for 224 seconds, but contact ceased just before the retrorockets were to fire, and the lander impacted at about 23.9 degrees south, 19.42 degrees west near Samara Valles.
The lander remains where it struck. NASA GISS Mars24 lists its impact coordinates, and the spacecraft is catalogued among the abandoned hardware on Mars.

sites.name: Deep Space 2 microprobes
sites.coordNote: Impact location published by NASA GISS Mars24 lander catalogue (75 S, 163.5 W); no signal was received from the microprobes.
sites.summary: Deep Space 2's two microprobes were meant to penetrate the south polar cap in 1999 — they hit at 75 S, 163.5 W and never answered.
narrative: Deep Space 2 carried two microprobes aboard Mars Polar Lander to penetrate the Martian south polar cap. On 3 December 1999 the microprobes separated and impacted at about 75 degrees south, 163.5 degrees west in Planum Australe, but no signal was ever received.
The microprobes remain where they struck, listed by NASA GISS Mars24 alongside Mars Polar Lander.

sites.name: Ingenuity helicopter wreck
sites.categoryDetail: Rotorcraft wreck — first powered flight on another planet
sites.status: Mission complete — helicopter wreck remains on surface
sites.coordNote: Final landing location published by NASA for Ingenuity's 72nd flight in Jezero Crater; wreck imaged by Perseverance.
sites.summary: Ingenuity made 72 flights on Mars, then crashed in Jezero Crater in 2024 — its wreck sits at 18.535 N, 77.447 E.
narrative: Ingenuity arrived at Mars aboard Perseverance in February 2021 and became the first powered, controlled flight on another planet. It flew 72 times, scouting ahead of the rover.

On its 72nd flight on 25 January 2024, Ingenuity's rotor blades were damaged and it made a hard landing in Jezero Crater at 18.535 degrees north, 77.447 degrees east. Perseverance imaged the wreck, which remains on the surface as the first aircraft wreck on another planet.
